name: Aquib Ali Zarwari
role: Senior PPP-equivalent politician — sits above Jamali in the political hierarchy
real_life_inspiration: Barely-disguised Asif Ali Zardari — husband of Benazir Bhutto, PPP co-chairman, and President of Pakistan (2008–2013). The name 'Zarwari' is a single-letter variant of 'Zardari'. His PPP relied heavily on Lyari's gang-controlled vote bank for decades.

inspiration_notes.zardari_parallel: Asif Ali Zardari is one of Pakistan's most powerful political figures. His PPP's relationship with Lyari's criminal networks is well-documented — Lyari reliably delivered PPP votes in exchange for political protection of gang operations. This was an open secret in Pakistani politics.
inspiration_notes.bhutto_dynasty_context: Zardari became President after the assassination of Benazir Bhutto (December 2007) and the PPP's subsequent 2008 election victory. His presidency (2008-2013) coincides exactly with the Film 1 Act 3 / 26/11 era, making him the political patron-in-chief of Lyari's criminal network at the time of the Mumbai attacks.
inspiration_notes.film_function: Zarwari represents the apex of the political protection racket — above Jamali, he is why Jamali can operate with impunity. He is the reason the Dakait-Jamali link is politically protected at the highest level.
inspiration_notes.oracle_note: Highest-capability political actor on the Pakistani civilian side. Not an active adversary (no operational role) but the structural condition that enables all the political-criminal nexus below him. In SNA terms: the highest-betweenness political node.
